# Complexity Changes by Version

Every built-in function has a **complexity** cost, charged against a script's complexity limit. Several built-ins get cheaper (rarely, more expensive) at a later standard library version, with no change to their arguments or return type, so a script recompiled at a higher `STDLIB_VERSION` can pass where it previously failed the complexity limit, with no code change.

```{note}
Generated from node-scala commit [`104ddc70e8`](https://github.com/Decentral-America/node-scala/tree/104ddc70e8007175e0d1306b6db527ad37bb1b1f) by `docs/scripts/generate_ride_reference.py`. The generator reads the compiled standard library the node evaluates scripts with, not the Scala source text, so every cost on this page is the one the node charges. To change this page, change the generator or move it to a newer node-scala commit and regenerate. CI fails on any hand edit.
```

The table lists every function whose cost differs anywhere between V5 and V9: 74 rows, one per overload. A dash means the function does not exist at that version. Functions that are new in V6 to V9 appear here only if their cost changes after they are added; for everything a version adds, see {doc}`Standard Library Versions <08_stdlib-versions>`, and for the full list of functions and costs at one version, see the {doc}`function reference <13_function-reference/index>`.

Where a function's argument types are written differently at different versions, the row shows the newest spelling. For example, `rsaVerify` takes the digest algorithm as `RsaDigestAlgs` up to V5 and as the equivalent spelled-out union from V6.
